candidate.source_title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units

candidate.name: Layer normalization
candidate.causal_claim: LayerNorm stabilizes the Transformer blocks GPT-2 stacks (moved to pre-norm in GPT-2); it arrives inside the inherited GPT-1 architecture, not as a separately consumed result.
candidate.definition: Normalization method (Ba, Kiros & Hinton, 2016) normalizing layer activations per example, stabilizing recurrent and deep training.
candidate.source_title: Layer Normalization

candidate.name: Adam optimizer
candidate.causal_claim: Adam is the optimizer family the GPT line trained with; a commodity component of the inherited training recipe, not a GPT-2-specific enabler.
candidate.definition: Optimizer (Kingma & Ba, 2014) with adaptive per-parameter rates from first/second moment estimates; became deep learning's default.
candidate.source_title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization

candidate.name: GELU activation
candidate.causal_claim: GELU is the activation the GPT line adopted from GPT-1 onward; it reaches GPT-2 inside the inherited architecture.
candidate.definition: Activation (Hendrycks & Gimpel, 2016) weighting inputs by their Gaussian CDF, adopted across Transformer models.
candidate.source_title: Gaussian Error Linear Units (GELUs)

candidate.name: BooksCorpus
candidate.causal_claim: BooksCorpus was GPT-1's pretraining corpus - the data half of the recipe GPT-2 replaced with WebText; its channel runs through GPT-1.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Zhu et al., 2015) of 11,038 unpublished books (~74M sentences) used to train the original GPT.
candidate.source_title: Aligning Books and Movies: Towards Story-like Visual Explanations by Watching Movies and Reading Books

candidate.name: Common Crawl
candidate.causal_claim: Common Crawl is the web-scale corpus infrastructure of the era; GPT-2's WebText was deliberately NOT Common Crawl (Reddit-linked pages instead), so the channel is weak.
candidate.definition: Nonprofit web archive (founded 2007-08) providing petabytes of crawled web pages used to train many LMs.
candidate.source_title: Common Crawl

candidate.name: AlexNet
candidate.causal_claim: AlexNet opened the deep-learning era whose scaling logic GPT-2 extends to language; it reaches GPT-2 through the entire deep-learning succession, not directly.
candidate.definition: CNN (Krizhevsky, Sutskever & Hinton, 2012) winning ImageNet by a wide margin with GPU training, founding the deep-learning era.
candidate.source_title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

candidate.name: CUDA GPU computing
candidate.causal_claim: CUDA made the GPU training of every model in this lineage practical; it reaches GPT-2 as inherited infrastructure, two successions removed.
candidate.definition: Platform (NVIDIA, 2007) exposing GPU parallelism to general computation, the substrate of deep-learning training economics.
candidate.source_title: CUDA

candidate.name: Backpropagation
candidate.causal_claim: Backpropagation trained every network in the lineage; it reaches GPT-2 through the models and recipes that embody it.
candidate.definition: Algorithm (Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams, 1986) computing gradients through layered networks by the chain rule.
candidate.source_title: Backpropagation

candidate.name: LSTM
candidate.causal_claim: LSTMs were the pre-Transformer LM substrate (ELMo, ULMFiT); GPT-2's lineage displaced them via the Transformer, which is the channel.
candidate.definition: Recurrent architecture (Hochreiter & Schmidhuber, 1997) with gated memory cells for long-range sequence learning.
candidate.source_title: Long short-term memory

candidate.name: Sequence-to-sequence learning
candidate.causal_claim: Seq2seq founded neural sequence transduction; it reaches GPT-2 through the Transformer that displaced it.
candidate.definition: Framework (Sutskever et al., 2014) mapping sequences to sequences with LSTM encoder-decoders.
candidate.source_title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks

candidate.name: Bahdanau attention
candidate.causal_claim: Bahdanau attention is the Transformer's own predecessor; it reaches GPT-2 inside self-attention, via the Transformer.
candidate.definition: Mechanism (Bahdanau et al., 2014) letting a decoder attend over encoder states in neural MT.
candidate.source_title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate

candidate.name: Matching Networks
candidate.causal_claim: Matching Networks did one-shot classification by attention over support examples - a conditioning-flavored few-shot method, but embedding-based and never consumed by the GPT line.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Vinyals et al., 2016) for one-shot learning via attention over a support set in embedding space.
candidate.source_title: Matching Networks for One Shot Learning

candidate.name: Zero-shot learning via attributes
candidate.causal_claim: Attribute-based zero-shot classification in vision showed category transfer without examples a decade earlier - a conceptual sibling in another modality, with no channel into GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Method (Lampert, Nickisch & Harmeling, 2009) classifying unseen animal classes via human-specified attribute vectors.
candidate.source_title: Learning to detect unseen object classes by between-class attribute transfer

candidate.name: Kneser-Ney smoothing
candidate.causal_claim: Kneser-Ney was the statistical-LM state of the art the neural lineage displaced; ancestry of the task, not of the method.
candidate.definition: Smoothing technique (Kneser & Ney, 1995) for n-gram LMs, the best-performing backoff scheme of the statistical era.
candidate.source_title: Kneser-Ney smoothing

candidate.name: Perplexity as LM metric
candidate.causal_claim: Perplexity (Jelinek-era) is the yardstick GPT-2's log-linear scaling claim is stated in; a measurement convention, not an enabler of the capability.
candidate.definition: Metric from speech-recognition LM evaluation (Jelinek, 1970s): exponentiated cross-entropy of a test set under the model.
candidate.source_title: Perplexity

candidate.name: One Billion Word Benchmark
candidate.causal_claim: The 1B Word Benchmark standardized neural LM comparison in the pre-Transformer years; part of the evaluation lineage, not an input to GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Benchmark (Chelba et al., 2013) for statistical language modeling at billion-word scale.
candidate.source_title: One Billion Word Benchmark for Measuring Progress in Statistical Language Modeling

candidate.name: Penn Treebank LM benchmark
candidate.causal_claim: PTB was the small-data LM testbed of the neural-LM era (Mikolov's RNNLM results); evaluation ancestry only.
candidate.definition: Corpus (Marcus et al., 1993) whose LM split became the standard small benchmark for neural language models.
candidate.source_title: Penn Treebank

candidate.name: TensorFlow
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-1/GPT-2 were implemented in TensorFlow; commodity tooling any equivalent framework replaces, not a milestone in the method's causal chain.
candidate.definition: Google's open-source deep-learning framework (2015) for dataflow graph computation.
candidate.source_title: TensorFlow

candidate.name: PyTorch
candidate.causal_claim: PyTorch was the era's other framework; the GPT line's public code was TensorFlow-based, so even the tooling channel points elsewhere.
candidate.definition: Facebook's open-source deep-learning framework (2016) with dynamic computation graphs.
candidate.source_title: PyTorch

candidate.name: Distributed training (parameter servers)
candidate.causal_claim: Large-scale distributed training patterns underpin all big-model runs of the era; GPT-2's 1.5B training was modest by later standards and consumed no specific distributed-training milestone.
candidate.definition: Architecture pattern (Li et al., 2014) scaling ML training across clusters via parameter servers.
candidate.source_title: Scaling Distributed Machine Learning with the Parameter Server

candidate.name: Curriculum learning
candidate.causal_claim: Curriculum learning orders training examples easy-to-hard; GPT-2's training used no curriculum - a named idea in the training-methods space with no channel.
candidate.definition: Strategy (Bengio et al., 2009) presenting training examples in a meaningful order to improve generalization and speed.
candidate.source_title: Curriculum Learning

candidate.name: Generating sequences with RNNs (Graves)
candidate.causal_claim: Graves 2013 showed RNNs generating convincing text and handwriting sample-by-sample - the generative-LM demonstration tradition GPT-2 scales; ancestry through the neural-LM lineage.
candidate.definition: Work (Graves, 2013) using LSTMs with mixture-density outputs to generate handwriting and text sequences.
candidate.source_title: Generating Sequences With Recurrent Neural Networks

candidate.name: GloVe
candidate.causal_claim: GloVe was the other embedding standard of the word2vec era; the embedding premise reaches GPT-2 through the pretraining tradition, and GPT-2 learns its embeddings end-to-end regardless.
candidate.definition: Embedding method (Pennington, Socher & Manning, 2014) factorizing global co-occurrence statistics.
candidate.source_title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation

candidate.name: Fast weights (Schmidhuber)
candidate.causal_claim: Schmidhuber's fast-weight programmers proposed one network programming another via weight changes - a conceptual ancestor of conditioning, cited by later meta-learning, with no channel into GPT-2's work.
candidate.definition: Proposal (Schmidhuber, 1992) in which a slow network generates fast weights for another network, an early form of learned adaptation.
candidate.source_title: Learning to Control Fast-Weight Memories: An Alternative to Dynamic Recurrent Networks

candidate.name: Learning to learn (Thrun & Pratt)
candidate.causal_claim: The learning-to-learn literature framed transfer as meta-knowledge decades before; framing ancestry for few-shot claims, not a consumed component.
candidate.definition: Research programme (Thrun & Pratt, eds., 1998) on learning inductive bias from task families.
candidate.source_title: Learning to Learn

candidate.name: Neural Turing Machines
candidate.causal_claim: NTMs coupled networks to external memory; an alternative augmentation direction that the GPT lineage did not take.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Graves et al., 2014) giving a neural controller differentiable read/write access to an external memory bank.
candidate.source_title: Neural Turing Machines

candidate.name: Memory Networks
candidate.causal_claim: Memory Networks answered questions over an explicit memory store; a sibling QA architecture with no channel into GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Weston, Chopra & Bordes, 2014) combining learned representations with a long-term memory component for QA.
candidate.source_title: Memory Networks

candidate.name: End-to-End Memory Networks
candidate.causal_claim: MemN2N made memory attention end-to-end differentiable; part of the attention-era QA landscape, not GPT-2's lineage.
candidate.definition: Model (Sukhbaatar et al., 2015) reading memory with multiple attention hops, trained end-to-end.
candidate.source_title: End-To-End Memory Networks

candidate.name: Differentiable Neural Computer
candidate.causal_claim: The DNC was DeepMind's flagship memory-augmented architecture; a parallel direction with no channel into the GPT line.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Graves et al., 2016) coupling a neural controller to an external memory matrix with differentiable addressing.
candidate.source_title: Hybrid computing using a neural network with dynamic external memory

candidate.name: Residual networks (ResNet)
candidate.causal_claim: Residual connections are inside every Transformer block GPT-2 stacks; they arrive as part of the Transformer/GPT-1 architecture, not as a separately consumed result.
candidate.definition: Architecture (He et al., 2015) with skip connections enabling training of 100+ layer networks, winning ImageNet 2015.
candidate.source_title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition

candidate.name: Dropout
candidate.causal_claim: Dropout is a standard regularizer inside the inherited training recipe; commodity component, not a GPT-2 enabler in the milestone sense.
candidate.definition: Regularization technique (Srivastava et al., 2014) randomly dropping units during training to prevent co-adaptation.
candidate.source_title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting

candidate.name: Batch normalization
candidate.causal_claim: BatchNorm normalized activations across batches; the Transformer line standardized on LayerNorm instead, so even the component channel points to its sibling.
candidate.definition: Method (Ioffe & Szegedy, 2015) normalizing layer inputs per mini-batch, accelerating deep training.
candidate.source_title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift

candidate.name: Weight initialization (Xavier/He)
candidate.causal_claim: Principled initialization is inside every training run of the era; background technique, not a milestone GPT-2 distinctively consumed (GPT-2's scaled residual init is its own tweak).
candidate.definition: Initialization schemes (Glorot & Bengio, 2010; He et al., 2015) keeping activation/gradient scales stable across layers.
candidate.source_title: Understanding the difficulty of training deep feedforward neural networks

candidate.name: Stochastic gradient descent with momentum
candidate.causal_claim: SGD is the optimization substrate of all of it; it reaches GPT-2 through every intervening training run and belongs many levels deeper in the trace.
candidate.definition: Optimization method (stochastic approximation, Robbins-Monro 1951; momentum, Polyak 1964) training models by noisy gradient steps.
candidate.source_title: Stochastic gradient descent

candidate.name: Automatic differentiation (autodiff)
candidate.causal_claim: Autodiff (Linnainmaa 1970; framework-era reverse mode) is how gradients are computed in practice; deep infrastructure ancestry, mediated by every framework and model above it.
candidate.definition: Technique (Linnainmaa, 1970) computing derivatives of composite functions by the chain rule in reverse accumulation order.
candidate.source_title: Automatic differentiation

candidate.name: Theano
candidate.causal_claim: Theano pioneered symbolic autodiff frameworks for research; GPT-2's stack was TensorFlow, so even the tooling lineage is a sibling.
candidate.definition: Python library (Bergstra et al., 2007-2010) for symbolic tensor computation and GPU code generation, from MILA.
candidate.source_title: Theano (software)

candidate.name: cuDNN
candidate.causal_claim: cuDNN's GPU kernels underlie all framework training of the era; commodity plumbing beneath the recipe, not a consumed milestone.
candidate.definition: NVIDIA library (2014) of GPU-accelerated primitives for deep neural networks.
candidate.source_title: cuDNN

candidate.name: Data parallelism and model parallelism practice
candidate.causal_claim: Multi-GPU training practice (from AlexNet's two-GPU split onward) is the era's background capability; GPT-2's 1.5B run consumed the practice generically, not a named milestone.
candidate.definition: Practice of splitting training across GPUs (Krizhevsky, 2012 onward), scaling to data/model parallelism in large runs.
candidate.source_title: One weird trick for parallelizing convolutional neural networks

member_names: Data parallelism and model parallelism practice

candidate.name: Reddit as a curated data source
candidate.causal_claim: WebText's curation trick was scraping pages linked from Reddit with karma>=3 - a data choice inside GPT-2's own contribution, using a commodity platform; the platform is not a milestone predecessor.
candidate.definition: Social news platform (founded 2005) whose outbound links and karma scores OpenAI used as a quality filter for WebText.
candidate.source_title: Reddit

member_names: Reddit as a curated data source

candidate.name: Wikipedia as training corpus
candidate.causal_claim: Wikipedia text trained half the models of the era; GPT-2's WebText notably drew on Reddit-linked pages broadly - corpus plumbing, not a milestone in the method's chain.
candidate.definition: Free encyclopedia (founded 2001) whose text became a standard LM training and evaluation corpus.
candidate.source_title: Wikipedia

candidate.name: Shannon's n-gram entropy studies
candidate.causal_claim: Shannon's prediction-and-entropy work founded language modeling as a measurable science; the remotest task ancestry, mediated by the entire statistical and neural LM succession.
candidate.definition: Studies (Shannon, 1951) estimating the entropy of English via human prediction experiments, founding statistical language modeling.
candidate.source_title: Prediction and Entropy of Printed English

candidate.name: Markov chains for text
candidate.causal_claim: Markov's letter-sequence analysis of Pushkin is the first statistical text model; ancestry of the task across a century of intermediaries.
candidate.definition: Analysis (Markov, 1913) of vowel/consonant sequences in Eugene Onegin, the first application of Markov chains to text.
candidate.source_title: Markov chain

candidate.name: Feedforward neural LM (Bengio follow-ups)
candidate.causal_claim: Duplicate-angle variant of the NPLM line (already scouted as the neural probabilistic LM); dedupe is expected to merge or drop it.
candidate.definition: The 2003 JMLR neural LM and its immediate follow-up literature establishing feedforward neural language modeling.
candidate.source_title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model

candidate.name: Hierarchical softmax and NCE
candidate.causal_claim: Output-layer approximations made large-vocabulary neural LMs trainable in the Mikolov era; GPT-2's full softmax at 50k vocab on modern hardware no longer needed them - a displaced enabling trick of the prior era.
candidate.definition: Techniques (Morin & Bengio, 2005; Mnih & Teh, 2012; Gutmann & Hyvarinen, 2010) approximating the softmax partition function for large vocabularies.
candidate.source_title: Noise-contrastive estimation

candidate.name: Character-aware LM (Kim et al.)
candidate.causal_claim: Character-CNN word models addressed open vocabularies compositionally; the GPT line solved the same problem with BPE instead - a sibling solution, not a channel.
candidate.definition: Model (Kim et al., 2015) composing word representations from character CNNs for language modeling.
candidate.source_title: Character-Aware Neural Language Models

candidate.name: Pointer-sentinel and variational LM advances
candidate.causal_claim: Mid-2010s PTB-era LM refinements (pointer sentinel, variational dropout) mark the RNN-LM era's ceiling that the Transformer succession displaced; no channel into GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Models (Merity et al., 2016; Gal & Ghahramani, 2016) pushing RNN LM perplexity via pointer mechanisms and variational dropout.
candidate.source_title: Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models

candidate.name: Semi-supervised sequence learning
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: Dai & Le's sequence-autoencoding pretraining anticipated LM pretraining for classification in 2015; an early paradigm ancestor whose channel runs through the 2018 wave.
candidate.definition: Method (Dai & Le, 2015) pretraining sequence models by LM/autoencoding before supervised fine-tuning, improving classification.
candidate.source_title: Semi-supervised Sequence Learning

candidate.name: LAMBADA
candidate.causal_claim: LAMBADA was a headline zero-shot test in GPT-2's paper (accuracy jumping with scale); a testbed the result was measured on, not a component of the method.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Paperno et al., 2016) of narrative passages whose final word requires broad discourse context, designed to defeat local-context models.
candidate.source_title: The LAMBADA dataset: Word prediction requiring a broad discourse context

candidate.name: Children's Book Test
candidate.causal_claim: CBT was among GPT-2's zero-shot evaluation suites; evaluation ancestry only.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Hill et al., 2015/2016) of children's-book sentences with a missing word to predict from context, for evaluating reading models.
candidate.source_title: The Goldilocks Principle: Reading Children's Books with Explicit Memory Representations

candidate.name: WikiText
candidate.causal_claim: WikiText-103 was a standard LM benchmark in GPT-2's zero-shot perplexity tables; a yardstick, not an enabler.
candidate.definition: Benchmark (Merity et al., 2016) of 103M tokens from verified Wikipedia articles for long-term LM evaluation.
candidate.source_title: Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models

candidate.name: CNN/Daily Mail summarization dataset
candidate.causal_claim: CNN/Daily Mail was the corpus for GPT-2's zero-shot summarization probe (TL;DR prompting); evaluation lineage only.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Hermann et al., 2015) of news articles with bullet summaries, repurposed as the standard abstractive summarization benchmark.
candidate.source_title: Teaching Machines to Read and Comprehend

candidate.name: Exploring the Limits of Language Modeling
candidate.causal_claim: Jozefowicz et al. pushed LSTM LMs to their limits and catalogued what scale bought before Transformers - the immediate pre-history of the scaling question GPT-2 answered differently.
candidate.definition: Study (Jozefowicz et al., 2016) training very large LSTM LMs on the 1B Word Benchmark, analyzing architectures and output layers at scale.
candidate.source_title: Exploring the Limits of Language Modeling

member_names: Exploring the Limits of Language Modeling

candidate.name: WaveNet
candidate.causal_claim: WaveNet showed autoregressive generation at unprecedented fidelity in audio - the generative-modeling era's emblem, in another modality; no channel into GPT-2's text result.
candidate.definition: Generative model (van den Oord et al., 2016) of raw audio by dilated causal convolutions, transforming text-to-speech quality.
candidate.source_title: WaveNet: A Generative Model for Raw Audio

candidate.name: QRNN
candidate.causal_claim: QRNNs were the efficiency-focused RNN alternative of the PTB era; part of the displaced RNN-LM landscape, no channel into GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Bradbury et al., 2016) quasi-recurrent networks pooling convolutions across time for faster sequence modeling.
candidate.source_title: Quasi-Recurrent Neural Networks

candidate.name: Continuous cache and dynamic evaluation
candidate.causal_claim: Cache/dynamic-evaluation tricks squeezed RNN LMs by exploiting recency at test time; test-time adaptation ideas the GPT-2 demonstration did not use.
candidate.definition: Methods (Grave et al., 2016; Krause et al., 2017) improving LM perplexity via cache models and test-time gradient adaptation.
candidate.source_title: Improving Neural Language Models with a Continuous Cache

candidate.name: Winograd Schemas
candidate.causal_claim: Winograd schemas defined the commonsense coreference challenge used to probe LM understanding of the era; evaluation ancestry for GPT-2's claims.
candidate.definition: Challenge set (Levesque, 2011) of pronoun-resolution problems designed to require commonsense reasoning.
candidate.source_title: The Winograd Schema Challenge

candidate.name: Story Cloze and ROCStories
candidate.causal_claim: Story Cloze probed narrative understanding in the GPT-1-era evaluation suite; part of the task landscape, not an input to GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Benchmark (Mostafazadeh et al., 2016) choosing the right ending for five-sentence stories, over the ROCStories corpus.
candidate.source_title: A Corpus and Cloze Evaluation for Deeper Understanding of Commonsense Stories

candidate.name: Multi-task learning
candidate.problem_solved: Improved generalization by training related tasks together with shared representations.
candidate.scale_or_impact: The framework GPT-2's paper invoked for zero-shot transfer.

candidate.key_mechanism: 14M WordNet-organized images labeled via crowdsourcing.
candidate.lineage: Vision transfer precedent for NLP transfer learning.
candidate.name: ImageNet
candidate.problem_solved: Gave vision a million-scale labeled dataset that made pretraining transfer practical.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Pretrain-then-fine-tune in vision became the template NLP imported.

candidate.problem_solved: Learned generic sentence representations without labels.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Early unsupervised sentence-representation milestone.

candidate.key_mechanism: Entropy and n-gram statistics measure the predictability of symbol sequences.
candidate.name: Shannon information theory
candidate.problem_solved: Quantified information and prediction, founding statistical language modeling.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Foundation of information theory and LM evaluation.

candidate.key_mechanism: Conditional probabilities over word histories with smoothing and backoff.

candidate.problem_solved: Predicted words from fixed-order Markov statistics for speech recognition.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Standard LM technology for three decades.

candidate.name: Luong attention (effective approaches to attention-based NMT)
candidate.causal_claim: A refinement of Bahdanau attention; whatever it contributed to later attention practice arrived packaged in the Bahdanau attention mechanism it varies.

candidate.source_title: Effective Approaches to Attention-based Neural Machine Translation

member_names: Luong attention (effective approaches to attention-based NMT)

candidate.name: ByteNet
candidate.causal_claim: A parallel-computation rival to recurrence, but not an input to the Transformer's self-attention design.

candidate.source_title: ByteNet: A Convolutional Neural Network for Translation

candidate.name: Google's neural machine translation system (GNMT)
candidate.causal_claim: The recurrent state of the art the Transformer displaced - context and rival, not a consumed enabler.

candidate.name: Decomposable attention model (Parikh et al.)

candidate.name: Scheduled sampling

candidate.source_title: Scheduled Sampling for Sequence Prediction with Recurrent Neural Networks

candidate.name: ELMo

candidate.name: BERT
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: BERT is the encoder sibling of the 2018 pretraining wave - the alternative branch (masked, fine-tuned) to GPT-2's decoder, zero-shot branch; not consumed by GPT-2.

candidate.name: Deep learning scaling predictability (Hestness)
candidate.causal_claim: Hestness et al. showed learning curves follow predictable power laws with scale - the empirical backdrop for GPT-2's log-linear scaling bet, though GPT-2's paper derives its claim from its own runs.
candidate.definition: Study (Hestness et al., 2017) demonstrating predictable power-law scaling of model performance with data and model size across applications.
candidate.source_title: Deep Learning Scaling is Predictable, Empirically

candidate.name: MAML meta-learning
candidate.causal_claim: MAML learns initializations for fast few-shot adaptation by gradient steps - the meta-learning paradigm GPT-2's conditioning-based few-shot bypassed entirely; no channel, as with ICL's expansion.
candidate.definition: Meta-learning algorithm (Finn, Abbeel & Levine, 2017) learning parameter initializations adaptable to new tasks in a few gradient steps.
candidate.source_title: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Fast Adaptation of Deep Networks

candidate.name: Prototypical Networks
candidate.causal_claim: Prototypical Networks learn metric spaces for few-shot classification; part of the meta-learning paradigm with no channel into GPT-2's demonstration.

candidate.name: CoVe contextual vectors
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: CoVe transferred MT-encoder representations to downstream tasks, an early transfer-representation result in the run-up to ELMo/GPT-1; its channel runs through that 2018 wave.
candidate.definition: Representations (McCann et al., 2017) from a machine-translation encoder, improving classification and QA when concatenated with GloVe.

candidate.name: AWD-LSTM
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art

candidate.name: Contextual pre-training via language modeling (Peters 2017 NAACL)

candidate.name: CoQA
candidate.causal_claim: CoQA supplied GPT-2's flagship zero-shot number (55 F1 without task training); the stage for the demonstration, not an input to it.

candidate.name: RACE reading comprehension
candidate.causal_claim: RACE was part of the reading-comprehension evaluation landscape GPT-2's zero-shot claims were situated in; not an input.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Lai et al., 2017) of 100k English-exam questions for middle/high school students, for reading comprehension.
candidate.source_title: RACE: Large-scale ReAding Comprehension Dataset From Examinations

candidate.name: GLUE benchmark
candidate.causal_claim: GLUE defined the fine-tuning era's scoreboard that GPT-2's zero-shot stance implicitly argued against; the incumbent measurement regime, not an enabler.

candidate.name: ConvS2S
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art

candidate.name: Sparsely-Gated MoE
candidate.causal_claim: Shazeer's MoE scaled capacity via conditional computation - the road GPT-2 did not take (dense scaling); a sibling scaling philosophy with no channel.

candidate.name: Relative position encodings

candidate.name: Mixed-precision training

candidate.source_title: On the State of the Art of Evaluation in Neural Language Models

candidate.name: Exploring the Limits of Language Modeling
candidate.causal_claim: Jozefowicz et al. pushed LSTM LMs to their limits and catalogued what scale bought before Transformers - the immediate pre-history of the scaling question GPT-2 answered differently.
candidate.definition: Study (Jozefowicz et al., 2016) training very large LSTM LMs on the 1B Word Benchmark, analyzing architectures and output layers at scale.
candidate.source_title: Exploring the Limits of Language Modeling

member_names: Exploring the Limits of Language Modeling

candidate.name: WaveNet
candidate.causal_claim: WaveNet showed autoregressive generation at unprecedented fidelity in audio - the generative-modeling era's emblem, in another modality; no channel into GPT-2's text result.
candidate.definition: Generative model (van den Oord et al., 2016) of raw audio by dilated causal convolutions, transforming text-to-speech quality.
candidate.source_title: WaveNet: A Generative Model for Raw Audio

candidate.name: QRNN
candidate.causal_claim: QRNNs were the efficiency-focused RNN alternative of the PTB era; part of the displaced RNN-LM landscape, no channel into GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Bradbury et al., 2016) quasi-recurrent networks pooling convolutions across time for faster sequence modeling.
candidate.source_title: Quasi-Recurrent Neural Networks

candidate.name: Continuous cache and dynamic evaluation
candidate.causal_claim: Cache/dynamic-evaluation tricks squeezed RNN LMs by exploiting recency at test time; test-time adaptation ideas the GPT-2 demonstration did not use.
candidate.definition: Methods (Grave et al., 2016; Krause et al., 2017) improving LM perplexity via cache models and test-time gradient adaptation.
candidate.source_title: Improving Neural Language Models with a Continuous Cache

candidate.name: Winograd Schemas
candidate.causal_claim: Winograd schemas defined the commonsense coreference challenge used to probe LM understanding of the era; evaluation ancestry for GPT-2's claims.
candidate.definition: Challenge set (Levesque, 2011) of pronoun-resolution problems designed to require commonsense reasoning.
candidate.source_title: The Winograd Schema Challenge

candidate.name: Story Cloze and ROCStories
candidate.causal_claim: Story Cloze probed narrative understanding in the GPT-1-era evaluation suite; part of the task landscape, not an input to GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Benchmark (Mostafazadeh et al., 2016) choosing the right ending for five-sentence stories, over the ROCStories corpus.
candidate.source_title: A Corpus and Cloze Evaluation for Deeper Understanding of Commonsense Stories

candidate.name: TRPO (trust region policy optimization)
candidate.causal_claim: PPO's direct predecessor; the RLHF lineage consumed the simplified PPO, not TRPO itself.
candidate.definition: Algorithm (Schulman et al., 2015): policy updates constrained to a trust region via KL bound, with monotonic-improvement guarantees.
candidate.source_title: Trust Region Policy Optimization

candidate.name: Bradley-Terry model of paired comparisons
candidate.causal_claim: The preference-model form inside every RLHF reward model - but it reached RLHF packaged inside Christiano et al.'s reward-learning method.
candidate.definition: Statistical model (Bradley & Terry, 1952): probability that one item beats another is a logistic function of latent scores.
candidate.source_title: Rank Analysis of Incomplete Block Designs

candidate.name: Inverse reinforcement learning (Ng & Russell)
candidate.causal_claim: The intellectual ancestor of reward learning; RLHF's channel runs through preference-based reward learning (Christiano), not demonstration-based IRL.
candidate.definition: Framework (Ng & Russell, 2000): recover a reward function from an expert's observed behavior.
candidate.source_title: Algorithms for Inverse Reinforcement Learning

candidate.name: Apprenticeship learning via inverse RL (Abbeel & Ng)
candidate.causal_claim: A demonstration-based precursor; not the channel into preference-based RLHF.
candidate.definition: Method (Abbeel & Ng, 2004): match an expert's feature expectations to learn near-expert policies without a reward function.
candidate.source_title: Apprenticeship Learning via Inverse Reinforcement Learning

member_names: Apprenticeship learning via inverse RL (Abbeel & Ng)

candidate.name: TAMER framework (Knox & Stone)
candidate.causal_claim: An early human-feedback RL channel, but evaluative rather than preference-comparison based; the InstructGPT lineage runs through Christiano/Ziegler/Stiennon.
candidate.definition: Framework (Knox & Stone, 2009): agents learn from human evaluative feedback (+/-) treated as reward.
candidate.source_title: Interactively Shaping Agents via Human Reinforcement

candidate.name: TL;DR summarization dataset
candidate.causal_claim: The task substrate for Stiennon et al.'s demonstration - its channel into RLHF runs through that paper.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Reddit TL;DR posts with author-written summaries), used by Ziegler and Stiennon for RLHF summarization experiments.
candidate.source_title: TL;DR dataset (Reddit summarization corpus)

candidate.name: Reward shaping (Ng, Harada & Russell)
candidate.causal_claim: About hand-designed auxiliary rewards - a different mechanism from learning the reward itself.
candidate.definition: Theory (Ng, Harada & Russell, 1999): potential-based shaping rewards that speed learning without changing the optimal policy.
candidate.source_title: Policy Invariance Under Reward Transformations

candidate.name: Maximum entropy inverse RL (Ziebart)
candidate.causal_claim: An IRL refinement; its channel into preference-based reward learning runs through the IRL framework it extends.
candidate.definition: Method (Ziebart et al., 2008): probabilistic IRL matching feature expectations under a maximum-entropy distribution.
candidate.source_title: Maximum Entropy Inverse Reinforcement Learning

candidate.name: Bayesian inverse reinforcement learning (Ramachandran & Amir)
candidate.causal_claim: An IRL variant; mediated for Christiano via the IRL framework.
candidate.definition: Method (Ramachandran & Amir, 2007): maintain a posterior distribution over reward functions given demonstrations.
candidate.source_title: Bayesian Inverse Reinforcement Learning

card.definition: Framework (Sutskever et al., 2014) mapping sequences to sequences with LSTM encoder-decoders.

card.name: Semi-supervised sequence learning
card.definition: Method (Dai & Le, 2015) pretraining sequence models by LM/autoencoding before supervised fine-tuning, improving classification.

candidate.name: Generative pretraining (GPT-1)
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-1 is GPT-2's literal predecessor in the same lab: the Transformer-decoder generative-pretraining recipe GPT-2 scaled 10x and pushed from fine-tuning to zero-shot conditioning.
candidate.definition: OpenAI model (Radford et al., 2018): a 117M Transformer decoder pretrained on BooksCorpus, then fine-tuned per task, beating purpose-built models on 9 of 12 language-understanding tasks.
candidate.source_title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training

candidate.name: Transformer architecture
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-2 is a stack of Transformer decoder blocks; the architecture reaches it as part of the GPT-1 recipe it inherited and scaled.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Vaswani et al., 2017) replacing recurrence with self-attention; the substrate of all modern LLMs.
candidate.source_title: Attention Is All You Need

candidate.name: ULMFiT
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: ULMFiT proved pretrain-then-fine-tune for NLP months before GPT-1, defining the transfer paradigm GPT-2's zero-shot move reacted against and extended.
candidate.definition: Method (Howard & Ruder, 2018): LM pretraining, LM fine-tuning, classifier fine-tuning with discriminative rates and gradual unfreezing, large gains on text classification.
candidate.source_title: Universal Language Model Fine-tuning for Text Classification

candidate.name: ELMo
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: ELMo showed contextualized representations from a pretrained LM transfer broadly; part of the 2018 pretraining wave GPT-2's lineage runs through GPT-1, not ELMo's biLSTM design.
candidate.definition: Representation model (Peters et al., 2018): deep contextualized word vectors from a bidirectional LSTM LM, improving six NLP benchmarks.
candidate.source_title: Deep contextualized word representations

candidate.name: BERT
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: BERT is the encoder sibling of the 2018 pretraining wave - the alternative branch (masked, fine-tuned) to GPT-2's decoder, zero-shot branch; not consumed by GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Bidirectionally pretrained encoder (Devlin et al., 2018) whose fine-tuned representations reset NLP benchmarks.
candidate.source_title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

candidate.name: Deep learning scaling predictability (Hestness)
candidate.causal_claim: Hestness et al. showed learning curves follow predictable power laws with scale - the empirical backdrop for GPT-2's log-linear scaling bet, though GPT-2's paper derives its claim from its own runs.
candidate.definition: Study (Hestness et al., 2017) demonstrating predictable power-law scaling of model performance with data and model size across applications.
candidate.source_title: Deep Learning Scaling is Predictable, Empirically

candidate.name: MAML meta-learning
candidate.causal_claim: MAML learns initializations for fast few-shot adaptation by gradient steps - the meta-learning paradigm GPT-2's conditioning-based few-shot bypassed entirely; no channel, as with ICL's expansion.
candidate.definition: Meta-learning algorithm (Finn, Abbeel & Levine, 2017) learning parameter initializations adaptable to new tasks in a few gradient steps.
candidate.source_title: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Fast Adaptation of Deep Networks

candidate.name: Prototypical Networks
candidate.causal_claim: Prototypical Networks learn metric spaces for few-shot classification; part of the meta-learning paradigm with no channel into GPT-2's demonstration.
candidate.definition: Method (Snell, Swersky & Zemel, 2017) classifying by distance to class prototypes in a learned embedding space.
candidate.source_title: Prototypical Networks for Few-shot Learning

candidate.name: CoVe contextual vectors
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: CoVe transferred MT-encoder representations to downstream tasks, an early transfer-representation result in the run-up to ELMo/GPT-1; its channel runs through that 2018 wave.
candidate.definition: Representations (McCann et al., 2017) from a machine-translation encoder, improving classification and QA when concatenated with GloVe.
candidate.source_title: Learned in Translation: Contextualized Word Vectors

candidate.name: Transformer-XL
candidate.causal_claim: Transformer-XL extended context via recurrence in Jan 2019 - coeval with GPT-2 (same year), listed to be dropped by the year bound.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Dai et al., 2019) adding segment-level recurrence and relative positions to the Transformer for longer contexts.
candidate.source_title: Transformer-XL: Attentive Language Models Beyond a Fixed-Length Context

candidate.name: XLNet
candidate.causal_claim: XLNet's permutation LM was 2019's alternative pretraining objective - coeval with GPT-2, dropped by the year bound.
candidate.definition: Pretraining method (Yang et al., 2019) maximizing likelihood over permutation orders, combining autoregressive and autoencoding advantages.
candidate.source_title: XLNet: Generalized Autoregressive Pretraining for Language Understanding

candidate.name: RoBERTa
candidate.causal_claim: RoBERTa showed BERT was undertrained - a coeval 2019 replication study, dropped by the year bound.
candidate.definition: Study (Liu et al., 2019) optimizing BERT's training recipe for substantially better results.
candidate.source_title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach

candidate.name: ERNIE
candidate.causal_claim: Baidu's ERNIE added knowledge masking to pretraining in 2019 - coeval, dropped by the year bound.
candidate.definition: Pretraining model (Sun et al., 2019) masking entities and phrases to inject knowledge into representations.
candidate.source_title: ERNIE: Enhanced Representation through Knowledge Integration

candidate.name: GPT-2 staged release and 'too dangerous to release' debate
candidate.causal_claim: The staged-release controversy is part of GPT-2's own 2019 story, not a predecessor - coeval, dropped by the year bound.
candidate.definition: OpenAI's staged release of GPT-2 (Feb-Nov 2019) over misuse concerns, a landmark in release-policy debates.
candidate.source_title: GPT-2

candidate.name: AWD-LSTM
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: AWD-LSTM was the strongest RNN LM recipe ULMFiT built on; it reaches GPT-2 through the ULMFiT/GPT-1 paradigm succession, as a SUBTYPE-relative of the LSTM line.
candidate.definition: Regularized LSTM LM (Merity, Keskar & Socher, 2017) whose recipe powered ULMFiT's transfer results.
candidate.source_title: Regularizing and Optimizing LSTM Language Models

candidate.name: Contextual pre-training via language modeling (Peters 2017 NAACL)
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: The tagLM work preceding ELMo showed LM states helping sequence labelers; ancestry inside the ELMo branch of the 2018 wave.
candidate.definition: Work (Peters et al., 2017) augmenting sequence labelers with pretrained LM representations (tagLM), the direct run-up to ELMo.
candidate.source_title: Semi-supervised sequence tagging with bidirectional language models

candidate.name: CoQA
candidate.causal_claim: CoQA supplied GPT-2's flagship zero-shot number (55 F1 without task training); the stage for the demonstration, not an input to it.
candidate.definition: Conversational QA dataset (Reddy, Chen & Manning, 2018) of 127k questions over dialogues about passages, with rationale spans.
candidate.source_title: CoQA: A Conversational Question Answering Challenge

candidate.name: RACE reading comprehension
candidate.causal_claim: RACE was part of the reading-comprehension evaluation landscape GPT-2's zero-shot claims were situated in; not an input.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Lai et al., 2017) of 100k English-exam questions for middle/high school students, for reading comprehension.
candidate.source_title: RACE: Large-scale ReAding Comprehension Dataset From Examinations

candidate.name: GLUE benchmark
candidate.causal_claim: GLUE defined the fine-tuning era's scoreboard that GPT-2's zero-shot stance implicitly argued against; the incumbent measurement regime, not an enabler.
candidate.definition: Benchmark (Wang et al., 2018) of nine sentence-level understanding tasks that standardized transfer evaluation for BERT-era models.
candidate.source_title: GLUE: A Multi-Task Benchmark and Analysis Platform for Natural Language Understanding

candidate.name: ConvS2S
candidate.lens: immediate prior state of the art
candidate.causal_claim: Convolutional seq2seq was Facebook's parallel bet to the Transformer in 2017 - the sibling architecture line that lost; no channel into GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Gehring et al., 2017) using gated convolutions with attention for sequence-to-sequence tasks, matching RNN quality faster.
candidate.source_title: Convolutional Sequence to Sequence Learning

candidate.name: Sparsely-Gated MoE
candidate.causal_claim: Shazeer's MoE scaled capacity via conditional computation - the road GPT-2 did not take (dense scaling); a sibling scaling philosophy with no channel.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Shazeer et al., 2017) inserting sparsely-gated mixture-of-experts layers to reach 137B parameters with conditional compute.
candidate.source_title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer

candidate.name: Relative position encodings
candidate.causal_claim: Shaw et al.'s relative positions improved Transformer self-attention; GPT-2 used learned absolute positions from the GPT-1 design, so the component channel does not reach it.
candidate.definition: Method (Shaw, Uszkoreit & Vaswani, 2018) representing relative positions in self-attention, improving translation quality.
candidate.source_title: Self-Attention with Relative Position Representations

candidate.name: Mixed-precision training
candidate.causal_claim: Mixed precision became standard large-training practice in this era; a generic technique GPT-2's run may have used but which no milestone claim attaches to.
candidate.definition: Technique (Micikevicius et al., 2017) training in FP16 with FP32 master weights, halving memory and speeding large runs.
candidate.source_title: Mixed Precision Training

candidate.name: AdamW and decoupled weight decay
candidate.causal_claim: AdamW fixed weight decay in adaptive optimizers; the GPT line's runs used Adam-family training generically - a sibling refinement, not a consumed milestone.
candidate.definition: Method (Loshchilov & Hutter, 2017) decoupling weight decay from gradient-based updates in Adam, improving generalization.
candidate.source_title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization

candidate.name: On the State of the Art of Evaluation in Neural Language Models
candidate.causal_claim: Melis et al. showed tuned LSTMs rivaling newer architectures - the evaluation-hygiene debate framing GPT-2's era; commentary, not a component.
candidate.definition: Study (Melis, Dyer & Blunsom, 2017) demonstrating standard LSTM LMs with tuned hyperparameters match or beat newer architectures.
candidate.source_title: On the State of the Art of Evaluation in Neural Language Models

candidate.name: MultiNLI
candidate.causal_claim: MultiNLI was a flagship transfer task of the GPT-1 fine-tuning demonstration; GPT-2's zero-shot stance bypassed the fine-tune eval regime it belongs to.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Williams, Nangia & Bowman, 2017) of 433k sentence pairs for natural language inference across genres.
candidate.source_title: A Broad-Coverage Challenge Corpus for Sentence Understanding through Inference

candidate.name: GPT-2
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-3 is GPT-2 scaled ~100x: same decoder architecture, same BPE tokenizer, same conditioning-based task specification - the paper's model section is explicitly GPT-2's design at larger scale.
candidate.definition: OpenAI model (Radford et al., 2019): 1.5B Transformer decoder trained on WebText, demonstrating zero-shot task transfer by conditioning.
candidate.source_title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners

candidate.name: Sparse Transformer
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-3's paper states it uses 'alternating dense and locally banded sparse attention patterns in the layers of the transformer, similar to the Sparse Transformer' - a directly consumed architectural component.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Child et al., 2019, OpenAI): factorized strided+local attention patterns reducing self-attention complexity for long sequences.
candidate.source_title: Sparse attention - LLM Wiki

candidate.name: Megatron-LM
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-3 required model parallelism at 175B; Megatron-LM is the prominent 2019 demonstration of tensor parallelism - but no record shows GPT-3's training consumed NVIDIA's implementation rather than OpenAI's own.
candidate.definition: NVIDIA framework (Shoeybi et al., 2019): intra-layer tensor model parallelism for training multi-billion-parameter Transformers.
candidate.source_title: Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism

candidate.name: Scaling laws for neural language models (Kaplan et al.)
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-3's 175B size choice follows the Kaplan scaling-law analysis from the same lab months earlier - coeval at year granularity.
candidate.definition: Empirical study (Kaplan et al., Jan 2020, OpenAI): loss follows power laws in model size, data, and compute, prescribing much larger models.
candidate.source_title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models

candidate.name: CTRL conditional language model
candidate.causal_claim: A parallel demonstration of steerable large LMs; not part of GPT-3's lineage.
candidate.definition: Model (Keskar et al., 2019, Salesforce): 1.6B LM steered by control codes.
candidate.source_title: CTRL: A Conditional Transformer Language Model for Controllable Generation

candidate.name: T5 text-to-text transfer Transformer
candidate.causal_claim: A parallel pretraining paradigm (fine-tune per task); GPT-3's paper contrasts its in-context approach rather than consuming T5.
candidate.definition: Model/framework (Raffel et al., 2019, Google): unified text-to-text format with encoder-decoder Transformer pretrained on C4.
candidate.source_title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer

candidate.name: SuperGLUE benchmark
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-3 was evaluated on SuperGLUE few-shot; an evaluation target, not an enabler of the leap.
candidate.definition: Benchmark suite (Wang et al., 2019) of hard language-understanding tasks.
candidate.source_title: SuperGLUE: A Stickier Benchmark for General-Purpose Language Understanding Systems

candidate.name: Natural Questions dataset
candidate.causal_claim: A GPT-3 few-shot evaluation set, not an enabler.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019, Google): real search queries with Wikipedia answers.
candidate.source_title: Natural Questions: A Benchmark for Question Answering Research

candidate.name: Winogrande dataset
candidate.causal_claim: A GPT-3 evaluation set, not an enabler.
candidate.definition: Dataset (Sakaguchi et al., 2019): large-scale Winograd-style commonsense benchmark.
candidate.source_title: Winogrande: An Adversarial Winograd Schema Challenge at Scale

candidate.name: WebText corpus
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-3 trained on WebText2, an expanded version of GPT-2's WebText - the channel runs through GPT-2.
candidate.definition: Dataset (OpenAI, 2019): web pages from outbound Reddit links, built for GPT-2.
candidate.source_title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners

candidate.name: Microsoft-OpenAI Azure supercomputing partnership
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-3's training run executed on the Microsoft-built cluster - an institutional/compute precondition rather than a technical milestone in the lineage.
candidate.definition: Partnership (announced Jul 2019): Microsoft invested $1B in OpenAI to build Azure AI supercomputing for large-model training.
candidate.source_title: Microsoft invests in OpenAI (2019 announcement)

candidate.name: DeepSpeed ZeRO optimizer
candidate.causal_claim: Coeval with GPT-3 (2020); not part of GPT-3's training stack on the record.
candidate.definition: Library (Rajbhandari et al., 2020, Microsoft): memory-optimization for distributed training.
candidate.source_title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models

candidate.name: ELECTRA
candidate.causal_claim: Coeval with GPT-3 (2020) and a parallel paradigm.
candidate.definition: Model (Clark et al., 2020, Google): replaced-token-detection pretraining.
candidate.source_title: ELECTRA: Pre-training Text Encoders as Discriminators Rather Than Generators

candidate.name: Reformer
candidate.causal_claim: Coeval with GPT-3 (2020); not consumed by it.
candidate.definition: Architecture (Kitaev et al., 2020): LSH attention and reversible layers for efficient Transformers.
candidate.source_title: Reformer: The Efficient Transformer

candidate.name: Deep RL from human preferences (Christiano et al.)
candidate.causal_claim: Christiano-style preference learning directly enabled the agent's leap as the first demonstration that human comparisons could train a reward model guiding behavior — the seed of RLHF.
candidate.source_title: Why is ChatGPT so good? (Scale AI)
candidate.definition: Method (Christiano et al., 2017) learning a reward model from human preferences over trajectory segments and optimizing it with RL.

candidate.name: PPO (proximal policy optimization)
candidate.causal_claim: PPO directly enabled the agent's leap as the optimization algorithm that ran the RLHF stage aligning the agent's engine.
candidate.source_title: The Day We Stopped Predicting the Next Word: How ChatGPT Was Actually Built
candidate.definition: Policy-gradient RL algorithm (Schulman et al., 2017) with clipped surrogate objective; the standard optimizer for RLHF.

candidate.name: Large-scale pretraining (GPT-3)
candidate.causal_claim: GPT-3-scale pretraining directly enabled the agent's leap by producing a single model with enough world knowledge and few-shot adaptability to serve as a general task engine.
candidate.source_title: AI Paper Review: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback
candidate.definition: Training very large autoregressive language models on web-scale text; GPT-3 (175B) showed few-shot in-context task performance without fine-tuning.

candidate.name: Fine-tuning language models from human preferences (Ziegler et al.)
candidate.causal_claim: The first application of preference-based reward learning to language models - the direct methodological bridge between Christiano et al. 2017 and Stiennon et al. 2020 / InstructGPT.
candidate.definition: Method (Ziegler et al., 2019, OpenAI): train a reward model from human comparisons and fine-tune a pretrained LM (GPT-2) with PPO under a KL penalty.
candidate.source_title: Fine-Tuning Language Models from Human Preferences - ADS

candidate.name: Learning to summarize from human feedback (Stiennon et al.)
candidate.causal_claim: The immediate predecessor of InstructGPT: same recipe, same lab, six shared authors; proved RLHF beats supervised baselines and human reference summaries.
candidate.definition: Method (Stiennon et al., 2020, OpenAI): full RLHF recipe - human comparisons, Bradley-Terry reward model, PPO with reference-KL penalty - applied to summarization at 1.3B-6.7B scale.
candidate.source_title: Learning to summarize from human feedback

candidate.name: Preference-based reinforcement learning (Wirth et al.)
candidate.causal_claim: The formal backdrop Christiano et al. operationalized at deep-RL scale in the same year; the consumed artifact in the lineage is Christiano's method.
candidate.definition: Survey/formalization (Wirth et al., 2017) of RL from trajectory preferences rather than numeric rewards.
candidate.source_title: Preference-Based Reinforcement Learning: A Formal Framework and a Survey

candidate.name: WebGPT
candidate.causal_claim: A sibling application of human-feedback fine-tuning, not an enabler of the RLHF recipe itself.
candidate.definition: System (Nakano et al., 2021, OpenAI): GPT-3 fine-tuned with human feedback to answer questions using a text browser.
candidate.source_title: WebGPT: Browser-assisted question-answering with human feedback

candidate.name: InstructGPT
candidate.causal_claim: Coeval with the RLHF node itself (same year, same work) - cannot be its predecessor at year granularity.
candidate.definition: System (Ouyang et al., 2022, OpenAI): SFT + RLHF on GPT-3 - the very system this graph's RLHF node is drawn from.
candidate.source_title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback

candidate.name: Constitutional AI
candidate.causal_claim: Coeval with RLHF (2022) and a parallel branch, not a predecessor.
candidate.definition: Method (Bai et al., 2022, Anthropic): RL from AI feedback (RLAIF) using a written constitution.
candidate.source_title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback

candidate.name: Sparrow dialogue agent
candidate.causal_claim: Coeval with RLHF (2022); a parallel application.
candidate.definition: System (Glaese et al., 2022, DeepMind): dialogue agent trained with human judgements and rule-based rewards.
candidate.source_title: Improving alignment of dialogue agents via targeted human judgements

candidate.name: Direct preference optimization (DPO)
candidate.causal_claim: Postdates the RLHF node (2022) - a successor/simplification, not a predecessor.
candidate.definition: Method (Rafailov et al., 2023): optimize policies directly on preference data, bypassing an explicit reward model.
candidate.source_title: Direct Preference Optimization

candidate.name: COACH (convergent actor-critic by humans)
candidate.causal_claim: Coeval with Christiano et al. (2017) - a parallel human-feedback formulation, not a predecessor.
candidate.definition: Method (MacGlashan et al., 2017): human feedback interpreted as policy-dependent advantage rather than reward.
candidate.source_title: Interactive Learning from Policy-Dependent Human Feedback

candidate.name: Deep TAMER
candidate.causal_claim: Postdates Christiano et al. (2017).
candidate.definition: Method (Warnell et al., 2018): TAMER with deep function approximation for high-dimensional state spaces.
candidate.source_title: Deep TAMER: Interactive Agent Shaping in High-Dimensional State Spaces
